name: PixelTrail-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Frame 2 has the largest, most legible blocky pixel mass around the cursor.

tagline: Chunky white pixels bloom and fade along the pointer path.
summary: The pointer paints stair-stepped white squares onto a black panel; each burst holds a moment then dissolves, leaving a blocky trail behind the cursor.
appearance: A black panel with faint grey "Move your cursor" text. The pointer leaves a cluster of hard-edged white squares snapped to a coarse grid, forming stepped blocky clouds.
behaviour: Moving the pointer stamps pixels into a grid that widen into blocky clumps, then fade out over about a quarter of a second. Nothing moves unless the mouse moves.
demo_content: Faint hint text reading "Move your cursor".
search_phrases: white pixels painting on mouse move
use_when: A game, devtool or retro page wants a blocky cursor trail with arcade energy.
avoid_when: It only appears while the mouse moves, and the coarse white blocks can cover fine text.
customise: Grid size, trail radius, pixel lifetime, interpolation, easing, pixel colour and an optional gooey blur filter are props. There is no content.
weight_why: A small three.js canvas draws one shader plane and a 512-pixel trail texture.

a11y.note: Decorative and pointer-only; nothing appears for keyboard users and reduced-motion is not checked.

issues: The trail only exists while the pointer moves, so two frames show a bare panel.
Large pixel clumps can sit over the faint hint text and hide it.
polish_why: The blocky trail is clear and readable; the demo is bare black with a barely visible hint.
title: Pixel Cursor Trail
